A.explanation: Area OSTO is only the area under the straight part OS of the loading curve to T, not the work recovered on the full unloading path PQ.

B.explanation: Area OSPRO is the area under the loading curve OSP to R, which represents the work done on the wire by the applied force during stretching.

C.explanation: Area QPRQ is the area under the unloading curve PQ to the extension axis, which represents the elastic energy returned as work done by the wire during contraction.

D.explanation: Area OSPQO is the loop enclosed between loading OSP and unloading PQ, which represents the net work lost, not the work done by the wire on contraction.

hints: Notice the arrows: loading follows OSP outward from O to P, while unloading follows PQ inward from P to Q where extension remains.
Recall that on an $F$ against extension graph, work is the area between the curve and the extension axis.
To get work done by the wire, follow only the contraction path PQ from extension R back to Q and ask which shaded area lies under that curve.
walkthrough: Identify the two paths: OSP is stretching with extension increasing to R, and PQ is contraction with extension decreasing from R to Q.
State the rule: for a force-extension graph, work transferred is $W = \text{area under } F \text{ versus extension curve}$.
Work done on the wire during loading is therefore the area under OSP down to the extension axis, bounded at R.
Work done by the wire during unloading is the area under the return curve PQ down to the extension axis, bounded between its end extensions Q and R.
That strip under PQ is labelled QPRQ, using the vertical PR at maximum extension and the point Q of zero force.
The loop OSPQO is the difference between loading and unloading areas, so it is energy dissipated, not energy returned. This is option C.
